To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) frequent subgraph mining applied to graph representations of proteins is a powerful method for finding spatial motifs that are characteristic of structural families; 2) the almost-Delauney edges provide an effective alternative to contact distance based edges in the graph representations of proteins; and 3) the patterns extracted from almost-Delauny graphs have a biological meaning equivalent to those extracted from distance-based graphs.
1. A novel frequent subgraph algorithm can be used to identify recurring spatial motifs in proteins.

(1) we have developed a new algorithm for extracting spatial packing motifs that are characteristic of proteins in a structural family; (2) we have used this algorithm to find such motifs in two protein families, and have shown that they are biologically meaningful; (3) we have shown that graph representations of proteins using almost-Delauney edges are as biologically informative as distance based graphs, and have a significant computational advantage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of graph-based approaches to the study of protein structural families.
the identification of recurring spatial patterns in protein structure, and we find that such patterns can be identified using graph representations of protein structure.

the problem of finding recurring patterns in protein structures, which we address by developing a novel algorithm that can be applied to different representations of protein structure, and by exploring the biological significance of the patterns found.

the almost-Delauney edges provide a good alternative to distance based edges in terms of biological interpretation, but the distance based edges are more robust and are recommended for practical use.

, for the protein structural family studied in this work, the almost-Delauney edge graph is an excellent representation for mining frequent subgraphs, and the frequent subgraphs extracted have biological relevance.

the spatial motifs identified in this paper are useful in characterizing the packing patterns of amino acid residues within protein structural families, and they may be useful in the development of methods for protein function prediction.

the spatial packing of amino-acid residues in proteins can be described in a compact and interpretable manner, and that the description can be used for protein classification.
